Why it matters

Your first AI leader will help shape your next two years.

This isn't only a technical hire. Long before anything ships, this person is working through decisions with you that get harder to revisit later.

Where they help

What gets built, and what doesn't

Which problems to tackle first, what to buy versus build, and what to set aside. Most of that gets worked out with you in their first quarter.

Where they help

Who you hire next

Your first AI leader helps you choose the next three. A strong one can reach people who wouldn't have taken the call otherwise.

Where they help

What your board hears about AI

They become your translator in the boardroom. How clearly they explain what's working, and what isn't, shapes every budget conversation that follows.

None of that shows up on a CV. It shows up in a conversation with someone who has done the job.

How we help

You don't just retain a search partner. You retain an expert.

Expertly is a retained search firm staffed by AI experts, people who have built and led AI inside real businesses. They work through the hire alongside you, from defining the role to agreeing the offer, and the thinking comes with the search rather than as a separate piece of consulting.

Before the search

We define the role with you

What has to be true in twelve months, who this person reports to, and which roles can wait. We work it out together before anyone writes a job description.

During the search

We find and assess them

Our experts approach the market directly and personally interview every finalist, then walk you through the reasoning behind each recommendation.

At the offer

We help you decide and close

Which of the final two or three to back, what number will actually be accepted, and how to set the role up so they say yes and stay.

The search

What a search firm gives you

  • The role, defined against your business, not a template borrowed from a tech giant's careers page.
  • The right people approached directly, by name, because our experts already know them.
  • Every finalist interviewed by an AI expert who has held the job you're hiring for.
  • A scorecard, a recommendation and the concerns, plus a debrief on how we got there.
The consulting

What you'd otherwise buy separately

  • Whether this hire is your right next step, or whether to wait a quarter and settle who owns the data first.
  • Build it or buy it, one central team or people embedded in each department.
  • Which problem to tackle first, and just as usefully, what to leave alone this year.
  • A number you can defend, based on what AI leaders are actually being offered and accepting right now.
Our process

Two people on your search, start to finish.

An AI expert who has led AI inside a business like yours, working with an account manager who keeps things moving and stays your point of contact. First call to shortlist usually runs two to three weeks.

Week one

The honest brief

Not the job description. What has to be true in twelve months, what has already been tried, and who inside the business this person has to win over.

Week one to two

Names, not applications

We go straight to the people already doing this well in your industry. You see who we're approaching, and why, before anyone is contacted.

Week two to three

Interviews that go deeper

Your expert takes every finalist through situations they have lived themselves, then tells you what each answer actually revealed.

At the offer

The decision

We help you weigh the final two or three, land on a number that will be accepted, and get it signed.

What step three produces

A scorecard written against your role.

Your AI expert scores every finalist on what decides whether an AI leader succeeds at your stage and in your industry, including the areas to watch, so you can plan around them before the offer goes out rather than discover them in month three.

Roles we place

Your first AI hire is usually one of these four.

Which one depends on where you are today. Working that out together is often the most useful half-hour of the whole process.

A few experiments, nobody owns it Head of Applied AI

Focus the work on the few ideas with a business owner and a number attached, stop the rest, and set a baseline you can measure against.

The demos are great, nothing is live Director of AI Engineering

Take one job people do every day and get it fully live, with someone's name on it, a way to switch it off, and a cost agreed up front.

One thing works, now everyone wants it VP of Artificial Intelligence

Turn that success into something other teams can reuse and run themselves. Half the job is technical; the other half is getting people to change how they work.

The business would notice if it stopped Chief AI Officer

Own AI the way a CFO owns money: know what's running, what it's exposed to, and have the authority to switch something off.
